text: DSH 插件 dsh-plugin-speech 为 Web 聊天中的助手回复提供朗读播放。它在每条已完成的助手消息操作区加入播放控制，并在常规设置中提供语音与朗读选项；宿主负责请求 Edge 文本转语音服务，浏览器接收并播放音频流。用户可以选择语音、调整语速音量和音高、试听样音，并设置是否跳过代码。朗读会保留链接文字并过滤表格、网址等非正文内容，适合希望免手阅读 DSH 回复或收听较长答复的用户。默认 Edge 提供方无需 API 密钥，但需要网络连接。

dsh-plugin-speech reads DSH Web replies aloud. It adds chat play controls and voice settings. The host sends text to Edge for synthesis; the browser plays streamed audio. Users can select voices, tune speech, preview samples, and skip code. Network access is needed; no API key is required.
想让 DSH 把助手的回答念出来，方便不看屏幕时收听。
有没有办法点击聊天回复后播放语音？
让 DSH 为生成的文字提供朗读和停止控制。
我希望调整朗读声音、语速和音高。
能不能先试听一个声音，再决定用哪个？
朗读回复时跳过代码块和表格可以吗？
I want DSH to read assistant replies aloud while I am away from the screen.
Can I play a chat response as speech and stop it with a control?
Let me preview voices and adjust speaking speed and pitch in DSH settings.
DSH 插件 dsh-plugin-speech 的功能「回复朗读」：在已完成的助手消息操作区提供播放控制，点击后将回复文本交给宿主合成并在浏览器播放，可再次停止。
DSH 插件 dsh-plugin-speech 的功能「语音设置」：常规设置栏可选择 Edge 语音、调整语速音量音高，并通过试听按钮播放样音；语音列表由宿主路由提供。
DSH 插件 dsh-plugin-speech 的功能「朗读文本整理」：发送合成前可跳过代码块和行内代码，并自动忽略表格、网址、图片及标记，只保留适合朗读的正文。
DSH 插件 dsh-plugin-speech 的功能「流式语音播放」：宿主将合成音频流回传给浏览器，浏览器边接收边播放；无法使用流式缓冲时仍可整段播放。
dsh-plugin-speech 使用前须知：朗读文本会发送到 speech.platform.bing.com 在线合成语音；默认 Edge 提供方无需 API Key，但需要网络连接。

@nakamuraia/dsh-plugin-speech README · dsh-plugin-speech：English | [中文](README.zh.md)

Read assistant replies aloud in [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness), one continuous voice per reply.

@nakamuraia/dsh-plugin-speech README · What it does：Each finished assistant message gets a play control in its action row. Press it and the reply is spoken through a text-to-speech service; press it again and it stops. A settings row in General owns the service, the voice, and the tuning.

@nakamuraia/dsh-plugin-speech README · What it does：The whole reply goes out in **one request** and the host streams the audio back while the service is still synthesizing it. The browser holds back only the first **1.5 seconds** of audio — enough to cover the first chunk's jitter — and starts the voice: measured at about **one second** from the click, with a two-minute reading arriving in under two seconds from then on.

@nakamuraia/dsh-plugin-speech README · Providers：| Service | Key needed | Voices |
|---|---|---|
| **Microsoft Edge** (default) | no | the service publishes its full catalog, every language it serves |

Adding a provider means adding one folder under `src/providers/` and one line in `src/providers/registry.ts` — the settings screen builds its fields from what the provider declares.

@nakamuraia/dsh-plugin-speech README · The Edge token：Every handshake carries a short-lived `Sec-MS-GEC` token: the current time in Windows file-time ticks, rounded down to five minutes, digested together with the well-known client token. In October 2026 the endpoint moved to a **second generation** of that token — a patched SHA-256 paired with a 64-bit checksum — and began answering the first generation with a bare `403` (`Edge TTS WebSocket error: Unexpected server response: 403`), which is what a reply that never speaks looks like from the browser. `src/providers/edge/gec.ts` reproduces the accepted generation; `server.ts` hands it to `msedge-tts` by replacing the library's private URL builder, which is also what pins the token version the endpoint now expects. If read-aloud stops working again, test that token first: it is the only part of this plugin that can expire without the code changing.

@nakamuraia/dsh-plugin-speech README · Requirements：- A DeepSeek Harness surface — `dsh web`, or the desktop app — version `0.2.0-rc.2` or newer.
- Network access to the speech service. Nothing else: there is no model to download, and the Edge provider needs no account.

@nakamuraia/dsh-plugin-speech README · Requirements：The version floor is not decorative. The plugin's preferences are its own Cordis entry config, exposed to the settings screen as a form through `ctx.configForms`. Releases before `0.2.0-rc.2` had plugins register settings namespaces themselves (`settings.register`) and handed the browser a `ctx.settingsScope`; both services are gone.

@nakamuraia/dsh-plugin-speech README · Install：This package declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, so it installs as a **profile bundle**: the package
manager links it, the launcher appends it to the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles`, and the
bundle's own patch layer inserts the plugin row. Installing also enables it — in DeepSeek
Harness, installing a plugin and enabling it in a profile are separate steps, and a bundle
collapses the two.

**Desktop app** — sidebar → **Plugins** → **Add plugin**, then give one of:

@nakamuraia/dsh-plugin-speech README · Install：- `@nakamuraia/dsh-plugin-speech` (the npm registry)
- `github:NakamuraIA/dsh-plugin-speech`
- an absolute path to a local checkout

**From the CLI** — the same operation, profile-scoped:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:NakamuraIA/dsh-plugin-speech
```

@nakamuraia/dsh-plugin-speech README · Install：Restart the surface afterwards. The host half claims its HTTP routes when the plugin loads,
a desktop profile is owned by the app, and a newly installed out-of-tree bundle is not mounted
by a live recomposition — an app-internal row added to a patch does reload immediately, a
package that has to come from the profile's `node_modules` does not.

@nakamuraia/dsh-plugin-speech README · One-off overlay, without installing：`cordis.patch.yml` is the same patch the bundle applies, so it also works as a temporary
command-line overlay:

```sh
dsh web --patch ./cordis.patch.yml
```

Do **not** do both. A profile patch that inserts `ui-speech` while the bundle is selected
collides with `duplicate loader entry id`; the profile layer is for overriding the row's
config, which is what the settings screen writes.

@nakamuraia/dsh-plugin-speech README · Settings：Settings opens on **General**, where a **Read aloud** row owns:

- **Service** — which provider speaks.
- **Language** and **Voice** — the catalog entry to use.
- **Speed**, **Volume**, **Pitch** — sent to the service with every request.
- **Skip code** — leave fenced code and inline code out of the reading.
- **Test voice** — speaks a sample through the settings on screen, saved or not.

@nakamuraia/dsh-plugin-speech README · Settings：The row edits the plugin's own entry config, so the chosen values persist in the profile patch beside the entry rather than in a settings document. Resetting a field restores the schema default, and a write the Host refuses leaves the stored value untouched while the row says so.

@nakamuraia/dsh-plugin-speech README · Settings：Tables and pasted spreadsheets are never read, whichever way **Skip code** is set. That switch decides only whether fenced and inline code are read: with it off, the code itself is spoken and just the fences go. Links keep their label and lose their target; emoji, quotes, and standalone symbols are dropped. Sentence punctuation is kept, because the voice uses it for pauses.

@nakamuraia/dsh-plugin-speech README · How it works：Synthesis lives on the host because a browser cannot hold an API key and cannot reach most services across CORS. The browser only posts text and plays bytes. Every editable leaf of the entry config is `.volatile()`, so a settings write lands in the running host without reloading it — the host reads the same value the browser wrote.

@nakamuraia/dsh-plugin-speech README · How it works：One request is the point. Every extra request pays a fresh handshake — around 0.9 s to the service — and adds a connection that can be dropped; sending the whole reply once means one handshake and one stream. The service is fast enough for that to be the right trade: measured at **73x realtime** on a warm connection and 1.5x on a cold one, so a two-minute reading arrives in under two seconds while the first second of it is already playing.

@nakamuraia/dsh-plugin-speech README · How it works：The 1.5-second head is the whole latency budget. It exists to cover the jitter between the first chunk and the next one, not to wait for a useful part of the reply: a smaller head starts playing on the first frame and occasionally stutters, a larger one buys nothing. If the stream dies after the voice started, what is already buffered still plays out; if the engine refuses the buffer outright the reply is played as one whole file instead.

@nakamuraia/dsh-plugin-speech README · How it works：A voice can also end every sentence with a long silence of its own — `pt-BR-AntonioNeural`, the schema default, leaves about 0.9 s at each one, while the multilingual voices leave none. That silence is in the audio the service returns, not in how this plugin plays it.

@nakamuraia/dsh-plugin-speech README · Development：This repository builds on its own against the published `@deepseek-ai/*` packages; no harness checkout is involved:

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm build      # tsc → lib/types, tsdown → lib/index.js + lib/client.js
pnpm test       # vitest
pnpm typecheck  # sources and specs

@nakamuraia/dsh-plugin-speech README · Development：`build/plugin-bundle.ts` is the client-bundle preset. It emits the `window.__ModuleLoader__.load` handoff, keeps every module-table row a `require`, compiles CSS Modules into one injected style tag, and fails the build on a cross-plugin value import. It is a self-contained copy of the harness preset, which is what lets the package be built here.

@nakamuraia/dsh-plugin-speech README · Development：Three specs under `tests/checkout/` compose the real client registries, which only exist as sources inside a harness checkout; `tests/checkout/README.md` explains why and how to run them. Everything else, including the client wiring, runs through `pnpm test`.

@nakamuraia/dsh-plugin-speech README · License：MIT. The Edge provider drives Microsoft's read-aloud endpoint through [`msedge-tts`](https://github.com/harvey-woo/msedge-tts) (MIT); that endpoint is not a documented, supported Microsoft API, so treat availability as best effort.
